Behind ThailandAddict is one person — a doctor who turns days off into trips, and trips into stories that are genuinely fun to read.
Behind-the-dorms lane packed with rice shops, spicy salads, grill-buffets, and small cafes, cheap and open late, the students' kitchen
Being a Chao Phraya riverside town, there's fresh freshwater fish — grilled, in tom yam, and deep-fried — at riverside spots and near the dam
Being a fishing town, it makes shrimp paste, fish sauce, salted fish, and dried seafood for sale, popular gifts that people stop to buy.
Being a student town means lots of cafes around the university and in the center — good for working or reading all day.
Being next to Korat, mee phat and noodle soups are easy to find around town, at friendly local prices.
Being on the Sakae Krang, the town has fresh freshwater fish straight from the cages — grilled fish, fish tom yum, and fried fish at the riverside restaurants.
Being right next to Udon Thani, you'll find khao piak sen and Vietnamese-style kuay jap around town. A hot, brothy breakfast.
